articles.title: Lakers star Luka Doncic’s 73-point outburst gets eye-opening comment from Quin Snyder
articles.summary: In his first season fully embracing the role of the Los Angeles Lakers’ franchise centerpiece after LeBron James’ departure, Luka Doncic has put together ext...
articles.body:
In his first season fully embracing the role of the Los Angeles Lakers ' franchise centerpiece after LeBron James' departure, Luka Doncic has put together extraordinary performances. His determination to guide the Lakers to as many victories as possible was on full display during Monday's 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks. His remarkable showing also won over the opposing coaching staff, as Quin Snyder had plenty of praise for the Lakers superstar.

During the postgame press conference, Snyder discussed Doncic's remarkable abilities and reflected on what it was like to be on the receiving end of his historic 73-point performance against the Hawks when he was playing for the Dallas Mavericks.

"I don't personalize that," Snyder said. "If I did, I guess it would be an honor. He's playing at a level that no one has seen in this league in a long, long time."

On Monday, Doncic once again spearheaded the Lakers' offensive attack after returning from lower-back tightness that forced him to miss Sunday's matchup against the Detroit Pistons.

The superstar guard made an immediate impact, finishing with 32 points, eight rebounds, and 10 assists to help Los Angeles secure another win. The Slovenian superstar has now recorded at least 30 points in eight of his first 10 games this season.

With that performance, Doncic also made Lakers history by becoming the first player in franchise history to record multiple games featuring at least 30 points, five assists, five steals, and two blocks. Only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Magic Johnson had previously reached that statistical combination.

The Lakers entered Monday's game without Austin Reaves, who was unavailable due to illness. However, Doncic's return, alongside valuable contributions from the supporting cast, allowed Los Angeles to overcome Reaves' absence and maintain its winning momentum.

With the victory, the Lakers improved their record to 10-2 while extending their winning streak to six consecutive games.

articles.title: La denuncia del atleta paralímpico Alberto Ávila: "Un acosador amenaza con reventarme y asesinar a mi madre"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño atiende a MARCA. Lleva desde mayo sufriendo acoso a través de las Redes sociales. El caso ya está en manos de las autoridades. Sospecha de alguien de su entorno
articles.summary: El madrileño atiende a MARCA. Lleva desde mayo sufriendo acoso a través de las Redes sociales. El caso ya está en manos de las autoridades. Sospecha de alguien de su entorno
articles.body: Alberto Ávila lleva desde mayo sufriendo acoso a través de sus Redes sociales, en las que acumula un millón y medio de seguidores entre TikTok e Instagram. El tono del acosador ha ido subiendo cada vez más hasta recibir amenazas contra su integridad física y la de su madre. El atleta paralímpico, que fue el primer concursante de Supervivientes con discapacidad, ya ha puesto en manos de las autoridades el caso. También lo ha denunciado en sus redes sociales. El madrileño atiende a MARCA para explicar lo sucedido. "Todo empezó a principios de mayo cuando una chica que conocía me dijo que le habían escrito por Redes diciéndole que nos habían visto juntos, que si yo tenía novia (no era verdad)... No le di importancia, pensé que era algo puntual. Pero se empezó a repetir este mismo patrón cada vez que empezaba a seguir a una chica en Instagram. Esa persona está obsesionada con las chicas a las que sigo", relata. Empezó a mosquearse cuando a finales de mayo ya eran eran cinco las chicas que le habían avisado de que una persona les había escrito diciéndole barbaridades sobre Alberto. "Siempre dejándome a mí como un guarro. Incluso les decía que me había visto traficando con drogas (que obviamente no es verdad), que soy un acosador…", rememora a MARCA. Y nos envía los pantallazos que lo demuestran. En su grupo de entrenamiento estaba su ex novia y el novio actual de ésta y ella le contó que también la estaba acosando a ella. El tono del acosador o acosadora, porque no sabe su género, fue subiendo con el paso del tiempo. En junio ya le amenazó directamente. “Me escribió: 'Sé dónde vives, ten huevos a salir a la calle que te voy a reventar. Voy a asesinar a tu madre”, confiesa. Y pasó de escribir a las chicas de su entorno a ampliar a su círculo más cercano para sonsacarles información. También le han llegado mensajes insultándole por su físico. "Cojito paleto. Deforme...". Ávila nació sin peroné, con una malformación de la pierna derecha. "Tiene de 30 a 40 cuentas falsas. Ha habido días que se ha creado tres cuentas en una hora. Yo no le doy bola, pero mis amigos o amigas que le han contestado han llegado a recibir 20 mensajes en 10 minutos", revela. Alberto alguna vez le ha respondido desde alguna cuenta falsa o de una amiga provocándole para sonsacarle información y una vez estuvo a punto de quedar en persona. Sospecha que es alguien de su entorno. "Sabe demasiados detalles de mi vida privada que es imposible que los conozca aunque me siga en Redes Sociales", cuenta. Porque en su perfil, Ávila no relata cada detalle de su vida sino que usa las Redes para normalizar y visibilizar la discapacidad a través del sentido del humor. Da algunos detalles que muestran el grado de obsesión de esa persona hacia él. "El 17 de septiembre salí por una discoteca en Segovia con dos amigos. Era un jueves, no lo sabía nadie porque yo no subí a mis redes nada de esa noche. Pues el acosador sabía que estaba allí porque al día siguiente me envió una foto diciéndome que me tenía vigilado", confiesa. A raíz de subir el vídeo a Instagram en el que mandaba un mensaje directamente a su acosador, le han escrito "un montón de chicas a las que llevo 5 ó 10 años sin ver, que a ellas también las había escrito". "Está denunciado, no le tengo miedo y sé que le van a acabar pillando tarde o temprano", avisa Ávila.

articles.title: 'I was looking forward to be in Magnus Carlsen's group': Vaishali after winning two blitz games against super GMs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Vaishali Rameshbabu made an impressive start at the inaugural Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Vaishali Rameshbabu made an impressive start at the inaugural Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest, defeating two well-known grandmasters, Hans Niemann and Wesley So, in the opening blitz event.Her victories were particularly significant as she is one of only two women competing in a 24-player field featuring some of the world's best chess players.Vaishali defeated Niemann in the first round before beating So in the third. Her win against So was especially impressive, as the American had recently claimed his fourth US Championship title.She eventually finished the nine-round blitz event with four points out of nine."I was looking forward to be in Magnus's group. It's a very strong group like Arjun, Wesley, MVL. I mean what a what a group this is. Yeah, it's going to be a lot of challenge. I'm looking forward," Vaishali told ChessBase India.Carlsen takes the lead in blitz eventMeanwhile, five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen dominated the opening event, finishing unbeaten with seven points from nine rounds. France's Maxime Vachier-Lagrave secured second place with 6.5 points, while Levon Aronian finished third with six points.Carlsen's final-round victory over Haik Martirosyan helped him secure the top spot. His strong finish also gives him an advantage in the next stages, as the tournament rules allow higher finishers to get better tiebreak positions and certain advantages in knockout matches.India's Arjun Erigaisi also had a promising run, defeating Vachier-Lagrave and Fabiano Caruana. However, a final-round loss to Aronian meant he finished with 5.5 points.Group stage brings a bigger challengeThe tournament will now move to the Fast Classic format, where 24 players will be divided into four groups of six. Each game will have 45 minutes on the clock, with an additional 30 seconds per move. A win will earn three points, while a draw will give each player one point.Vaishali and Bibisara Assaubayeva will compete in Group D alongside Vachier-Lagrave, Erigaisi, Niemann and So. Only the winners of the four groups will qualify for the main knockout stage.The $650,000 tournament is being organised as a pilot for a proposed world chess tour that will combine classical, rapid and blitz formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football Updated Rookie Report: Fernando Mendoza gets his shot
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Ray Garvin examines the progression of the 2026 rookie class as we head into the second half of the season.
articles.body:
Nine weeks into the NFL season, we've seen enough from this rookie class to know who's for real, who's still finding their footing and who could make some noise down the stretch. From Carnell Tate's impressive start in Tennessee to Fernando Mendoza getting his opportunity in Las Vegas, here's my midseason check-in on 15 rookies, and what I'm expecting for the rest of the season.

Carnell Tate has been everything we hoped he would be — and then some. Through seven games, he's hauled in 34 receptions for 413 yards and a touchdown despite playing in one of the more inconsistent passing offenses in football. Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans haven't exactly made life easy for their rookie receiver, but Tate continues to produce.

The talent is undeniable, the opportunity is there and the chemistry with Ward continues to develop. I expect Tate to build on what's already been a successful rookie campaign. He's a weekly fantasy starter with plenty of room to grow.

Jonah Coleman might be the rookie running back I'm most excited about for the second half of the season. He's rushed for 191 yards and three touchdowns while adding 13 receptions for another 128 yards. More importantly, look at how Denver is using him. He handled 21 touches in Week 9, and the coaching staff clearly trusts him.

With R.J. Harvey on injured reserve and J.K. Dobbins getting older, the opportunity is sitting right in front of Coleman. He's already shown he can contribute in the passing game and handle meaningful carries. I wouldn't be surprised if Coleman finishes as one of the most valuable rookie running backs in fantasy.

Omar Cooper Jr. missed time early in the season, but the moment he got healthy, he made his presence felt. Through four games, Cooper has 20 receptions for 306 yards and two touchdowns, including back-to-back 100-yard performances. In Week 9, he followed those outings with eight receptions for 58 yards while Garrett Wilson was sidelined.

What I've really liked is the rapport he's developing with Geno Smith. Cooper looks comfortable; he's earning opportunities and he's showing he can win in different areas of the field. Wilson's return could impact his volume, but I'm buying what we've seen. Cooper has legitimate weekly flex appeal moving forward.

KC Concepcion Jr. / Denzel Boston, WRs, Cleveland Browns

KC Concepcion Jr. has quietly been one of the most impressive rookie wide receivers. He's sitting at 37 receptions for 437 yards and a touchdown, including 251 receiving yards over his last three games. What jumps off the screen is his ability to create after the catch. Get this young man the football in space and let him work.

The Browns haven't exactly provided consistent quarterback play, but Concepcion continues to find ways to produce. He's dynamic, explosive and already showing flashes of a player who could eventually become a Pro Bowl-caliber receiver. For fantasy purposes, he's worked his way into weekly flex consideration.

And how about Denzel Boston? The rookie has 507 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 32 receptions. Boston gives me some young Mike Evans vibes with his size, downfield ability and willingness to go make contested catches. He's already producing explosive plays despite the limitations of this Browns offense.

What's encouraging is that both Boston and Concepcion are earning significant opportunities without cannibalizing each other's production. Boston has legitimate big-play upside every single week and continues to look like one of the steals of the rookie class. I love what we've seen and expect a strong finish.

Germie Bernard's rookie season has been a little up and down, but I've seen enough to remain encouraged. He's caught 32 passes for 284 yards and a touchdown, highlighted by a phenomenal 11-reception performance in Week 6. The following two games weren't nearly as productive, but I wouldn't let that discourage you.

Bernard has established himself as a trusted option for Aaron Rodgers in a Pittsburgh offense that's been better than advertised. His role makes sense. Get him the football quickly, let him operate in space and allow his natural ability to take over. Bernard feels like a buy-low candidate with a solid second-half outlook.

I can't believe I'm putting Fernando Mendoza on this list, but here we are. The No. 1 overall pick is taking over as the Raiders' starting quarterback after Kirk Cousins was traded to Minnesota . Mendoza has attempted just eight regular-season passes, completing six for 48 yards, so we have almost nothing to evaluate.

But here's what we do know: Cousins threw 20 touchdowns in nine games and Mendoza gets to operate in that same Klint Kubiak offense featuring Brock Bowers. Listen, any quarterback throwing to Brock Bowers gets a touchdown bonus in my book. Add Ashton Jeanty, Trey Tucker and a potentially more favorable schedule down the stretch, and there's legitimate streaming appeal here. I'm not expecting Mendoza to be a league winner, but don't be surprised if he becomes fantasy relevant sooner than people think.

Jadarian Price is one of those players where the box score doesn't tell the entire story. He's rushed for 172 yards and added 83 receiving yards on 10 catches without scoring a touchdown. The production hasn't been there consistently, but every time he touches the football, you see the explosiveness. Unfortunately, injuries and ball-security issues have limited his opportunities.

With Zach Charbonnet still working his way back from a knee injury, there's a path for Price to earn a larger role. Seattle's offensive line should also improve as it gets healthier. I'm cautiously optimistic, but I need to see him string together consistent performances before trusting him in fantasy lineups.

Makai Lemon has been better than his rookie numbers might suggest. Through nine games, he's caught 37 passes for 312 yards and one touchdown, including 19 receptions for 185 yards over his last three games. The Eagles offense has been difficult to watch at times, and Lemon has dealt with inconsistent quarterback play while occasionally being asked to operate as the team's top receiver with DeVonta Smith unavailable.

What I've loved is his ability to separate, particularly against zone coverage. He's consistently finding openings and earning targets. The big fantasy performances haven't arrived yet, but the underlying usage is encouraging. There's more here than the box score offers.

We finally got our first look at Jordyn Tyson, and while it wasn't perfect, there were encouraging signs. In his NFL debut, Tyson caught four passes for 30 yards but also lost a fumble on his first reception. I'm not worried about that. What matters is that New Orleans immediately looked to get him involved.

This Saints offense ranks among the league leaders in neutral-situation pass rate, meaning the opportunity should continue to be there. Getting Calvin Banks back should help Tyler Shough operate more comfortably behind that offensive line. The biggest question remains Tyson's health. If that hamstring holds up, I'm expecting his role to expand significantly.

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Mike Washington Jr. gave us one of the more surprising rookie performances of the season when he handled 25 carries for 83 yards. Then he turned around the following week and rushed six times for -3 yards. That's been the problem. Washington has 275 rushing yards and a touchdown this season, but his role remains difficult to project.

Neither Washington nor Ashton Jeanty has consistently found success running behind this Raiders offensive line. Washington clearly has some ability, but can this coaching staff establish a defined role for him? Until that happens, he's difficult to trust. He's an interesting stash with upside if Jeanty misses time.

There's no bigger fantasy disappointment from this rookie class than Jeremiyah Love. And before anybody gets upset, I'm not putting all of that on the player. Love has rushed for 268 yards, added just 36 receiving yards and scored two total touchdowns in six games. We've seen flashes of the talent that made him such a highly regarded prospect, but the situation in Arizona has been a disaster.

The offense has struggled, the quarterback situation has deteriorated and now Love is sitting on injured reserve. If you invested an early fantasy pick in him, there's no way around it — it's been disappointing. The talent hasn't disappeared, but the fantasy return simply hasn't been there.

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

Antonio Williams is one of those rookies who could become much more relevant over the second half of the season. He's caught 26 passes for 284 yards and a touchdown, including eight receptions for 79 yards over his last two games. The problem hasn't necessarily been Williams. It's been the Commanders' offense.

Jayden Daniels continues to deal with a significant elbow injury and Washington hasn't been particularly creative offensively. We've also seen Williams have some unfortunate plays wiped away. With Terry McLaurin out, there should be additional opportunities available. He's not a weekly fantasy starter yet, but there's a path for Williams to become a useful flex option.

Emmett Johnson has quietly put together 348 yards from scrimmage and two total touchdowns, including that ridiculous 128-yard receiving performance against Denver in Week 8. We saw a 73-yard touchdown reception and a player who can absolutely make things happen with the football in his hands.

The problem? Kenneth Walker III has been phenomenal since arriving in Kansas City.

Johnson isn't taking that starting job anytime soon. But what if the Chiefs can turn him into a Jerick McKinnon-type receiving weapon? There's potential for standalone fantasy value in that role. And if Walker were to miss time, Johnson immediately becomes one of the most valuable backups in football.

Kaelon Black has 303 rushing yards and a touchdown this season, and I don't think enough people are paying attention to what he's doing. That's more rushing production than Jeremiyah Love, Mike Washington Jr. and Jadarian Price. The biggest obstacle is obvious: Christian McCaffrey.

But we've seen San Francisco utilize multiple backs at times, and keeping McCaffrey fresh has to remain a priority. Black has demonstrated that he can be an effective runner when given opportunities. The receiving game hasn't been a major part of his role, so there are limitations to his standalone fantasy value. Still, this is a player I want rostered heading into the second half of the season.

articles.title: Four-star center commits to UConn men’s basketball, adding to strong ’27 class
articles.summary: The 2027 recruiting class is getting even stronger for the UConn men’s basketball program. Jack Thelen, a four-star, 7-foot-1 center from Osseo, Minnesota, a...
articles.body:
The 2027 recruiting class is getting even stronger for the UConn men's basketball program.

Jack Thelen, a four-star, 7-foot-1 center from Osseo, Minnesota, and Maple Grove High, announced his commitment to the Huskies via Rivals on Wednesday afternoon.

Thelen initially committed to Wisconsin in June but reopened his recruitment after seeing his stock rise over the summer. He averaged 8.5 points and 6.7 rebounds per game on the Adidas 3SSB circuit and climbed to the No. 16-ranked center in the class by 247Sports, No. 15 by ESPN . He's ranked No. 111 in the class in the 247Sports composite rankings.

Thelen earned an offer from Dan Hurley and staff after visiting Storrs on Oct. 29, and then visited Illinois on Nov. 7 before making his decision.

Thelen is the fourth recruit to choose UConn in the 2027 class, joining No. 10 recruit NaVorro Bowman Jr., a 6-foot-3 guard, and No. 11 recruit Jordan Page, a 6-foot-5 wing. The Huskies also landed a 6-foot-10 French center, Keny Vado, according to a report from Jonathan Givony earlier this month.

The four-man class ranks third nationally by 247Sports , behind only LSU and Houston.

"Thelen is a big bodied lefty with real size and a quality motor," 247Sports Director of Scouting, Adam Finkelstein, wrote . "He's got a definite competitive streak, is vocal on the defensive end, and willing to use his body in the lane. While he is sometimes content to trot the floor hunched over, he's not as vulnerable when pulled to the perimeter defensively as expected. Offensively, he doesn't appear to need a certain number of touches or shots to stay engaged. He has good hands, soft touch in the paint, both hands around the rim (albeit with a lower release point), is physical in the post, and reliable reversing the ball on the perimeter. While he's not looking to shoot out there yet, his 82% free-throw shooting is encouraging, even on very low volume (under 2 attempts per game)."

articles.title: Ex-Red Sox Reliever, Braves World Series Champion Retires After 11-Year MLB Career
articles.summary: Chris Martin has retired after 11 seasons in the big leagues
articles.body:
Longtime reliever Chris Martin has retired after 11 seasons in the big leagues, according to MLB insider Robert Murray.

Martin pitched for seven organizations, but spent the most time with the Texas Rangers. He also pitched for the Colorado Rockies, New York Yankees, Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Los Angeles Dodgers and Boston Red Sox.

Martin won a World Series with the Braves in 2021, pitching in five games during their run to the Fall Classic. He allowed just one run that postseason across 4 1/3 innings. He pitched in three postseasons for the Braves and one for the Dodgers.

The Rockies drafted Martin in 2005, but he did not make his debut until 2014, at 27 years old. He appeared in 16 games that season and was traded to the Yankees before the 2015 season. The Yankees released him after the 2015 season, and he spent the 2016 and 2017 seasons in Japan.

He appeared in 92 games for the Nippon-Ham Fighters in two seasons. In 2016, he had a 1.07 ERA, and in 2017 he had a 1.19 ERA. He signed with the Rangers before the 2018 season.

Since 2018, he has pitched in 394 games and posted a 3.26 ERA. He carved out a successful role as a reliever and even received Cy Young Award votes in 2023, when he was a member of the Red Sox.

The 40-year-old appeared in 16 games for the Rangers and pitched 14 innings. He had a 9.00 ERA, and now he has decided to hang it up.

In 2025, he posted a 2.98 ERA in 49 games, so his falloff was somewhat of a surprise. Regardless, his time in the big leagues has finally come to an end. He finished his career with a 3.53 ERA and pitched in a total of 434 games.

articles.title: Leon football Hall of Fame celebrates 50 years of history, tradition
articles.summary: Leon High School marks 50 years of its unique football Hall of Fame, a tradition started by coach Gene Cox.
articles.body:
For Kurt Unglaub , the significance of Leon High's Football Hall of Fame isn't simply the hundreds of former Lions who have been honored the past 50 years.

It's that the tradition started by legendary Leon football coach Gene Cox has endured.

While many similar programs have disappeared or evolved into broader athletic halls of fame, Leon's remains devoted solely to football and the people who built its tradition.

"Us being able to keep it going for 50 years, it's just been a work and just a blessing," Unglaub said. "I want you to know that, a huge blessing. … Fifty years of anything's pretty good."

That longevity will be celebrated Thursday at The Moon, where more than 300 people are expected to gather, including more than 80 Hall of Famers and dozens of former cheerleaders.

High school football changes. Coaches leave. Players grow older. But for five decades, the Leon Football Hall of Fame has kept its history, and the people who made it, connected.

"I don't know of any Hall of Fames in the state of Florida that have lasted that long," said Leon football coach Ricky Bell, one of three generations of his family in the Hall along with his father and son, Lions athletic director Riley Bell. "This has survived because it was set up the way it was set up in the beginning. And I think that really was some foresight on Gene Cox's thinking, so it would last and last."

Leon football Hall of Fame stirs fond memories

One reason Leon's football Hall of Fame is still going strong after 50 years can be traced to the way Cox helped structure it from the beginning.

Instead of tying the Hall's future to whoever happened to be Leon's head football coach, Cox helped establish an organization with its own officers, rotating leadership and regular meetings. That allowed new generations of former players and supporters to take ownership and keep the tradition alive through coaching and administrative changes.

Unglaub, a longtime member and former three-year president of the Leon Football Hall of Fame, was asked by the board to return as chairman of the 50th anniversary celebration.

He stressed that Thursday's event isn't a formal Hall of Fame ceremony but a reunion, bringing generations of Leon football players, coaches, cheerleaders and supporters back together.

Adding to the significance, Gene Cox's son, Alan, is serving as the board's president during the 50th anniversary year of a Hall of Fame that features more than 280 inductees.

"There's an 80-year-old cheerleader who is coming," Unglaub said. "We're not having a banquet. This is just a fun party. A celebration is what it is."

The 2026 season marks 110 years of the program, highlighted by a historic 37–31 double-overtime win against rival Lincoln High School that snapped a 27-year losing streak to the Trojans.

articles.title: Aday Mara’s Strong Development Defends Against OKC Injuries
articles.summary: Aday Mara is on the rise for the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, and the team hopes that he can continue his development throughout the campaign. Suddenly...
articles.body:
Aday Mara is on the rise for the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, and the team hopes that he can continue his development throughout the campaign. Suddenly thrown into the fire, it does seem that the big man is filling the gap in OKC's defensive needs. He's also shining on offense, which is definitely something they need with multiple key stars out with injuries for the Thunder .

From deterring opponents from scoring, blocking shots, crashing the glass, and even creating offensive opportunities, Mara has been a standout for Oklahoma City. He's providing a spark that you wouldn't expect from a rookie. Now he's proven that he can be a consistent player for the team, and that's the hope for him moving forward.

Now averaging 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game this season, it's clear that Mara has excelled off OKC's bench . His numbers have gone up, and he has garnered a higher usage rate than ever. That says a lot for someone who's supposed to be getting fewer touches as a reserve before getting acclimated to bigger minutes.

But with the Chet Holmgren injury , the Thunder's center spot finds itself with a vacant hole — something that Mara is now taking over in the star's absence. We are at a point where the Spanish center is showcasing his skill set well.

At seven-foot-three, OKC getting Mara in the draft was a huge boon for the franchise on both sides. He's got the potential to be a high-impact defensive anchor alongside Holmgren, which is on-brand with the Thunder's identity. Let's not forget the fact that he's just 21 as well.

As a big man, you'd expect Mara to be a hulk on the glass, much like Victor Wembanyama . This month, the Thunder center has finished with more than five boards in his games. He's averaging 7.8 rebounds in this month alone.

If that's not eye-catching enough for you, then it's worth noting that Mara's rebounding has been essential for the Thunder. In fact, thanks to his efforts, through 11 games, OKC is grabbing nearly five more defensive rebounds per game without Holmgren than with him (36.9 to 32.7). Of course, no Holmgren means Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein get more share at the center spot.

That's a huge difference in cleaning up the glass, which is considered a weakness for OKC by some. With Mara, it does seem that the team can still stay competitive on that end. Now imagine if Holmgren comes back and pairs up with Mara moving forward.

Mara's Shot-Blocking is Elite for a Rookie

To start off his career, Mara has logged 10 straight games with at least one block. He also leads all rookies in total blocks so far this season, which says a lot about his defensive prowess. Of course, some would say that it's less impressive given his height, but his level of hand-eye coordination at that height is hard to come by.

With 20 blocks into the season ( tied for fifth-most ) as of the time of writing, it's not inconceivable that he could receive DPOY votes in his rookie season. Being a reliable defender for OKC, a team that prides itself on defense, is a huge boost to his case.

At this point, he's probably knocking on the Rookie of the Year conversation, but that's still a long shot if we're going solely on his team having the best defense and having the most blocks among rookies.

Mara has so much to offer OKC this season. He's already shown that he can hit a triple on his first attempt (I-Hart has not made a single three in 28 attempts with the Thunder, mind you). Mara is expanding his game. He's shown flashes of playmaking, being able to go coast-to-coast when needed, and his superb shot-blocking ability makes him a huge asset for the team.

But we're just 11 games into the season, and there's so much more for Mara to play, and for OKC to learn how to use him best.

articles.title: Bucs pass rush gets encouraging boost from former first-round pick
articles.summary: Bucs pass rush gets encouraging boost from former first-round pick
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been waiting for their defensive line to consistently create disruption, and Calijah Kancey's performance against the Chicago Bears was an encouraging sign of what the former first-round pick can bring when he gets going. While Tampa Bay ultimately fell 27-24, Kancey was one of the defensive players who made life difficult for Caleb Williams, helping fuel a defensive performance that produced five turnovers. Kancey finished with three tackles and half a sack, but the numbers don't tell the whole story. His quickness and ability to penetrate the interior created problems for Chicago's offensive line, particularly as the game progressed. Kancey was consistently applying pressure and helped disrupt Williams' rhythm in the second half. After Chicago opened the game with two touchdown drives, Tampa Bay's defense settled in and made it increasingly difficult for Ben Johnson's offense to operate comfortably.

That is the type of impact the Buccaneers need from Kancey. His explosiveness off the snap has always been one of his biggest strengths, and his ability to attack gaps adds a different dimension to Tampa Bay's interior. At 6'1 and 281 pounds, he may not overpower every offensive lineman, but his first-step quickness and ability to get into the backfield can force quarterbacks off their intended spot. Kancey's development is particularly important as Tampa Bay looks for more consistency from its pass rush. He recorded 7.5 sacks in just 12 games during the 2024 season, showing the production he can deliver when healthy. After an injury-shortened 2025 campaign, getting him back to a meaningful level of disruption is a major positive for this defense.

Please submit your clips by the end of the day on Mondays each week to make sure your clip is potentially included to be a nominee.

We also have a step-to-step explainer , along with a link to the Journal Sentinel site, that explains how to upload your own highlight clips for nomination.

Wauwatosa East vs Whitefish Bay in WIAA Division 2 boys state soccer championship

Jeramani Denton, Saint Thomas More boys soccer

The junior forward scored one of the best goals of the WIAA boys soccer state tournament in the Division 3 state title match Saturday, Nov. 7. With the Cavaliers holding a 1-0 lead late in the first half of STM's 3-1 win over Edgerton , Denton fired a frozen rope of a right-footed strike into the upper 90 at the 35:56 mark to give STM a 2-0 lead on his 15th goal of the season.

Colin Gardner, sr., Racine Case football

Playing in the Division 1 state quarterfinal round for the first time in program history, Gardner drained the biggest kick in Racine Case lore with a walkoff 28-yard field goal as time expired to give the Eagles an improbable 6-3 victory over top-seeded Muskego on the road Friday, Nov. 6, to send Case to the state semifinals.

For the second time in program history in just its 11th year as a WIAA-certified high school, the Cristo Rey Jesuit Trailblazers won the D4 state title with a 2-1 victory over Lake Country Lutheran on Saturday, Nov. 7. The senior forward scored a wonderful goal in the final couple minutes of the first half, chipping the goaltender with a shot attempt a mile high through traffic that gave CRJ a 1-0 lead right before the halftime break for his 33rd goal of the campaign.

For the third time since 2022, Sussex Hamilton football is on the doorstep of playing for a Division 1 state title. The Chargers advanced to the state semifinal round with a 17-10 victory over defending state champion Arrowhead on the back of an outstanding go-ahead touchdown catch from Alex Restivo in the fourth quarter. The star senior made an amazing diving effort to haul in a Cole Erdmann pass late in the fourth that put Hamilton up for good.

articles.title: Dolphins not moving on from Malik Willis as their starting QB
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis landed on injured reserve with a groin injury on Tuesday, but he'll take his job back when he's ready.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis tried to play through a groin injury the last two weeks, but it was evident that the injury had limited his effectiveness, especially when it came to his mobility.

Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that the imaging revealed that the injury had progressed to the point that the medical staff believed Willis would need time off, which is why they placed him on injured reserve.

While Hafley did say that he hopes that Willis is back after the minimum four games, the quarterback is getting second opinions that could lead to surgery.

Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the team's starting quarterback going forward. However, Hafley told reporters that Willis will take his job back whenever he's healthy and in a position to lead the offense again.

Willis hasn't exactly played inspiring football even when he was healthy, and McCord could end up being a boost for Miami going forward. If that's the case, it would be tough to see the Dolphins switch back to Willis, especialy if McCord wins a couple games.

articles.title: South Knox girls basketball coach suspended for undue influence violation
articles.summary: The violation occurred in May, according to superintendent Jeff Cochren. Additionally, the program is on probation for the remainder of the season.
articles.body:
South Knox girls basketball coach Hollie Anson-Eaves has been suspended two games for violating the Indiana High School Athletic Association's undue influence policy, superintendent Jeff Cochren confirmed Wednesday. Additionally, the program has been placed on probation for the remainder of the season.

Rule 20-1 of the IHSAA bylaws prohibits the recruitment or attempted recruitment of a prospective student through the use of undue influence, which is described as "the act of encouraging or inducing a prospective student to attend a school for athletic purposes."

Anson-Eaves may resume coaching after serving her two-game suspension, but, according to the IHSAA by-laws, must immediately file a report with the IHSAA outlining any corrective actions taken or to be taken by the coach.

In an email to IndyStar and The Courier Press, Cochren said the violation occurred some time in May 2026. The South Knox administration was informed of "the potential for a violation" by the IHSAA in July, and was then "required to respond" to the alleged violation. They did so via written letter in August, then received official notification of the punishment on Nov. 5.

Cochren did not immediately respond to a request for further comment regarding the violation itself.

Anson-Eaves served the first game of her suspension Tuesday, sitting out South Knox's 62-47 win over Class 3A Washington. The Spartans travel to Corydon Central this weekend for the Cluckers Battle at the First Capital. They open the two-day, three-game event against Evansville Central on Friday night.

When reached for comment, an IHSAA spokesperson said per their policy, they do not comment on rules violations or suspensions and instead leave it up to the school if they wish to offer a response.

South Knox added one transfer from Vincennes over the summer, sophomore Azaria Easley, who played for the soccer team in the fall.

Jesse Easley, Azaria's father, addressed allegations of recruiting by SK in a public Facebook post , stating the decision to transfer was rooted in concerns with the Vincennes Lincoln girls soccer program.

Opponents are allowed to drop the Spartans from their 2026-27 schedule without penalty, per IHSAA Bylaw Rule 9-16(b) (3), if alleged to violate Rule 20 concerning undue influence.

Two teams have already canceled games with South Knox: Sectional foe Eastern Greene, its season-opening opponent (Nov. 7), and Vincennes Lincoln, which was scheduled for Jan. 16.

The Spartans have picked up a game vs. Evansville Reitz and is working to add another game to its schedule, according to Cochren.

Anson-Eaves, who will return to the sidelines following her two-game suspension (expected to return Saturday), is 195-114 in 13 seasons at South Knox, with three sectional titles and a Class 2A state championship (2025).

The Spartans are among the favorites to win 2A this season, boasting a veteran lineup headlined by Indiana All-Star candidate Kendal Hill , who averaged 19.2 points, 10.3 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 4.3 steals. Seniors Grace Detweiler, Ellie Burke, Kalissa Lavely and Laya Thomas, and juniors Zoe Glimore and Brynley Millspaugh round out the list of returners.

articles.title: O'Shea proud of how team-mates handled Israel games
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea said he is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.

During a four-game Nations League schedule, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side lost away to Kosovo and drew at home to Austria - who they are preparing to face in return fixtures - but it was two games against Israel which tested their resolve.

O'Shea stepped in as captain in the absence of injured skipper Nathan Collins and the 27-year-old acknowledged it "was a tough situation to be in" as they faced Israel in two games on neutral territory.

The first of those resulted in a 3-0 victory for the Irish in Hungary, a game that looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

The sides drew 1-1 in the second meeting in Serbia and, while the saga proved a challenge for all within the Republic of Ireland squad, O'Shea - who missed the second game for personal reasons - paid tribute to his team-mates for the support he received as stand-in skipper.

"I think I was quite lucky, I am really proud to be part of the group, with some great people in it," said the Ipswich Town captain.

"Even the players playing now as well, they are great leaders themselves. I never felt I was fully alone in having to do anything

"There were always people around me. I always keep level-headed, I don't get too high with the highs or too low with the lows."

He added: "Of course it was a difficult time, it was a time that I had to learn stuff about myself, how I was going to react to things. But I think as a group we did excellently.

"It was a tough situation to be in, but we overcame it as best we could. And I am really proud of the group and the staff."

'Great to have Collins and Coleman back'

Collins is back to lead the team for Saturday's trip to face Austria in Linz and the final League B3 game at home to Kosovo on Tuesday (both 19:45 GMT).

Also part of the squad is Seamus Coleman, who has taken on a 'hybrid role' despite not being named in manager Hallgrimsson's official 24-man squad.

"It's great to have them [Collins and Coleman] back," O'Shea continued.

"It would have been great if they were there in the last camp as well, but we had some really good people in that last camp who were doing great things.

"Nathan's the captain, so it's always great to have him back in. Seamus' knowledge is so, so valuable to us. I think we are a stronger group when we have them two with us."

Coleman has been without a club since leaving Everton at the end of last season, following 17 years with the Toffees.

The 38-year-old defender recently said he is considering retirement but Republic of Ireland assistant coach John O'Shea is delighted to have the Donegal man around the squad.

"It's us helping Seamus and Seamus helping us," O'Shea said of Coleman's role on the training pitch.

"To see the impact he's having, the quality that remains in his ability and the driving and pushing he's doing for everyone in the group has been good to see. Not much has changed."

articles.title: Panthers replenish practice squad after 2 players are poached by Dolphins, Titans
articles.summary: After having two of their players poached, the Panthers added back to their practice squad on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers were quick to replenish their practice squad on Wednesday.

This morning, defensive tackle Keith Cooper Jr. and linebacker Mohamoud Diabate were signed off the team's practice squad by the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans, respectively. Carolina then turned around to add wide receiver David Moore and defensive tackle Cam Horsley to the group.

Moore, who was released yesterday , has spent the past three seasons with the Panthers. His first two campaigns saw him record 33 catches for 356 yards and three touchdowns over 21 games.

He's made six appearances here in 2026, with most of his work coming on special teams. The 31-year-old veteran has fielded four punts for 31 yards and eight kickoffs for 168 yards.

Horsley, an undrafted free agent from 2025, split his first two seasons between the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals . The 6-foot-3, 312-pounder played in one game as a rookie.

articles.title: Are the Wizards Asking Too Much of Kyshawn George?
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become. Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wiza...
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become.

Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wizards, but his recent performances have also raised questions about whether the Wizards are putting too much responsibility on him too soon.

George has shown that he can help this team in several areas of the game. The 6-foot-7 forward has become a key piece of the Wizards' offense, using his scoring ability and creative playmaking to make opportunities for himself and his teammates.

Over the last few games, George has become particularly encouraging. George scored 22 points against the Orlando Magic on Nov. 2, followed by 25 points facing the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 4. He then dropped 33 points in another loss to Atlanta the next game, adding eight assists and five three-pointers.

Those numbers show why Washington has continued to give George opportunities with the ball in his hands. However, his development isn't just about scoring and how many points he can score. The Wizards also need to find the right role for him as he continues to improve in the NBA.

Finding the Right Role for Kyshawn George

One of Kyshawn George's biggest strengths has been his versatility. He's been able to score, defend multiple positions, and help create offense for his teammates. Washington has also been experimenting with using him as a point guard when Trae Young is not playing.

That responsibility has not always been easy.

George recorded eight turnovers against the Toronto Raptors on Oct. 23, a performance that showed some of the challenges of asking him to run the Wizards' offense. He has the ability to make plays, but becoming a good ball handler takes time.

After George's 22-point performance on the Chicago Bulls defense on Oct. 24, Wizards coach Brian Keefe discussed his ability to create more opportunities by getting into the paint.

"You saw him being able to create and get into the paint," Keefe said. "A lot more paint touches for us tonight, which we wanted to emphasize, and he was a catalyst for that."

The comments, reported by Roundtable Sports , show that Washington finds value in what George can bring when he is attacking the basket instead of forcing himself to make all of the plays.

The Wizards should continue giving him opportunities to handle the ball, but they should also recognize when he's most effective.

Trae Young's presence could play an important role in George's development. As an experienced point guard, Young can help take pressure off George while giving him chances to contribute as a secondary playmaker.

George doesn't need to become the team's primary ball handler to be an important part of the offense. Playing alongside Trae Young can allow him to focus on scoring, attacking the basket, and making decisions when defenses give him opportunities.

Washington has also shown that George can help lead the offense when Young is not on the floor. That flexibility is important, especially for a team that is still trying to establish its offensive identity.

The challenge is finding a balance between giving George more responsibility and allowing him to play to his strengths.

The Wizards have invested in developing young players, and George is becoming one of the more important parts of that process. Washington has exercised his fourth-year team option on Nov. 1, showing commitment to keeping him in the team's long-term process.

Through the Wizards' first 11 games, George is averaging 17.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game.

Still, his recent performances shouldn't mean the Wizards expect him to carry the team every night. George continues to develop as a scorer and playmaker, and there will be nights where he struggles.

Washington needs to give him room to make mistakes while putting him in positions where he can succeed more. Young can help take pressure off, while George continues learning how to become more consistent on offense.

George has shown that he deserves an important role in Washington. The next step the Wizards should take is making sure they can give him the right responsibilities to continue his development.

articles.title: New WWE Rumors on Bronson Reed Injury, Rollins Eyes WrestleMania Main Event & Enzo Fuels Return Buzz
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reported Details on Reed's Injuries Suffered at Crown Jewel

Bronson Reed reportedly did not make the trip back to the United States from Saudi Arabia after WWE Crown Jewel last weekend due to injuries suffered during the World Tag Team Championship match.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter , Reed suffered broken ribs and a punctured lung on a spot that saw Oba Femi throw him off the stage and through some tables.

That report came on the heels of Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp being the first to report that Reed had stayed back in Saudi Arabia due to the injury with a "top international executive and a member of [WWE's] medical team" accompanying him.

Reed did not technically wrestle a match at Crown Jewel, but he did get involved in the World Tag Team Championship bout pitting The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory against Penta and Je'Von Evans.

When Reed interfered, Femi showed up to neutralize him and tossed him off the stage and onto some tables.

That is reportedly the spot on which Reed's injuries occurred, rendering him unable to travel back home with the other WWE wrestlers and staff.

Reed only recently returned to action last month after missing about eight months with a torn bicep, which kept him off WrestleMania 42.

It is unclear what Reed's timeline for recovery is this time around, but there is little doubt that WWE would love to have him back in time for Royal Rumble in February and WrestleMania 43 in April at the very least.

Rollins Talks Desire to Headline WrestleMania Night 2

Seth Rollins has competed in the main event of Night 1 of WrestleMania on a couple of occasions, but he still has his sights set on an even loftier goal.

During an appearance this week on The Kittle Things with San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), Rollins declared, "I feel like I've never been in a main event of WrestleMania."

Rollins acknowledged that he was in Night 1 main events at WrestleMania 40 and WrestleMania 41, and he mentioned his Money in the Bank cash-in during the main event of WrestleMania 31 between Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar.

However, The Visionary feels like he still has some unfinished business as it relates to WrestleMania main events.

"I've had Night 1 main events, and I helped in the Night 2 main event at WrestleMania 40 with Cody [Rhodes] and Roman," Rollins said. "And I had the cash-in, but I've never been the person on the marquee to finish the show on Night 2.

"Mr. Triple H, let's work on that. Whoever's in charge. It's a tough sell. It's a tough sell. Maybe I've got a few years left. We'll see if I can get there."

To Rollins' point, he was not advertised for the main event of WrestleMania 31 despite technically being in the main event.

He actually opened that show against Randy Orton before cashing in his Money in the Bank contract during the bout between Reigns and Lesnar, and pinning Reigns to win the WWE Championship.

More recently, Rollins teamed with Rhodes against Reigns and The Rock in the Night 1 main event of WrestleMania, and he beat Reigns and CM Punk in the Triple Threat main event of Night 1 of WrestleMania 41.

On top of that, Rollins has competed in several other significant WrestleMania matches that weren't main events against the likes of Lesnar, Rhodes, Triple H, Kevin Owens and Logan Paul, among others.

A Night 2 may not be in the cards for Rollins at WrestleMania 43 in April since all signs are pointing toward Reigns vs. Femi, but he should have at least a few more opportunities to make it happen in the future.

In the midst of rumors and speculation regarding his WWE return, Enzo Amore cut a lengthy promo Tuesday on Instagram .

During the promo (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Amore dropped some intriguing lines, including "never say never," which is a line often uttered by pro wrestlers when asked about a potential WWE return.

Enzo also mentioned the "speculation" surrounding him, and closed out the video with the famous line he used at the end of his promos during his first run in WWE, spelling out "sawft," and punctuating it with, "How you doin'?"

A few months after his longtime tag team partner, Big Cass, made his return to WWE, Amore may be in line to do the same.

Last week, PWInsider.com (h/t Wrestle Ops ) reported that Enzo was believed to have signed with WWE "over the past week," and expected to be part of NXT.

Enzo was previously in WWE from 2012 to 2018, and he spent most of that time teaming with Cass in NXT and on the main roster.

However, near the end of his run, he became a singles star, holding the now-defunct Cruiserweight Championship twice.

Thanks largely to his next-level talking ability, Enzo proved he could hold his own as a singles wrestler during that time, which suggests he could have value in a similar role in NXT this time around.

articles.summary: Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz has been hospitalized after crashing during a practice lap ahead of Wednesday's Veterans Day Classic at Daytona International Speedway, according to Team Reaume and Entertainment Weekly.
articles.body:
Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz has been hospitalized after crashing during a practice lap ahead of Wednesday's Veterans Day Classic at Daytona International Speedway, according to Team Reaume and Entertainment Weekly .

"Frankie Muniz was involved in an incident while practicing for today's Proud to Honor event at Daytona International Speedway," Team Reaume said in a statement. "He was transported to a local medical facility for further evaluation. He is awake and alert."

Daytona was not open to the public at the time of Muniz's crash, according to Entertainment Weekly . A photo shared by Entertainment Weekly showed damage to the No. 30 Mustang Dark Horse R he was slated to drive.

Wednesday's race was set to feature Ford competitors racing in honor of the six military branches. Muniz was slated to represent the U.S. Air Force alongside Austin Cindric.

Muniz was involved in a crash earlier this season during an April NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series race at Bristol Motor Speedway but walked away from the incident.

Best known in his acting career for starring in Malcolm in the Middle, Muniz first raced in 2004 and restarted his career in 2021.

He competed full-time with Rette Jones Racing in ARCA Menards Series in 2023, then took over driving Reaume's No. 33 Ford in the Truck Series in 2025.

Muniz skipped multiple races from the Truck Series in October while winning the 2026 GT4 America Am championship title with co-driver Tyler Stone.

His best race of this NASCAR season came with a 12th-place finish at Talladega Superspeedway Oct. 23. Muniz most recently placed 25th at Martinsville Speedway Oct. 30.

articles.title: Secretary of Sport Says Canada Will Not Allow Russians to Play at World Junior Championships
articles.summary: OTTAWA, Ontario (AP) — Canada's Secretary of Sport says the country will not allow Russian players to compete at the upcoming world junior championships, even if they already hold valid visas.
articles.body:
OTTAWA, Ontario (AP) — Canada's Secretary of Sport says the country will not allow Russian players to compete at the upcoming world junior championships, even if they already hold valid visas.

Adam van Koeverden's statement Wednesday comes a week after the Canadian government threatened to supersede the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision to force the International Ice Hockey Federation to allow Russia back by refusing to offer visas for the tournament the country is hosting.

It was not immediately clear if the decision would put Norway back into the tournament for the best men's players under the age of 20 that is set to begin on Dec. 26 in the Canadian province of Alberta. Norway said last weekend it had been informed by the IIHF that it had been bumped from the world juniors to fit Russia, which had been banned since invading Ukraine in early 2022.

"These measures are not directed at the Russian and Belarusian people," van Koeverden said. "Rather, they are intended to prevent the governments of Russia and Belarus from using international sporting events hosted in Canada as platforms for state representation, political legitimacy and propaganda.

"Canada's position is unequivocal: As long as Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual. Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine."

Hockey Canada referred to statements last week when asked again about the latest development. A message sent to the IIHF seeking comment and clarification on the status of the final team in the field between Norway and Russia had not been returned.

articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo is known for his discipline, but his life away from football also has a delicious side. The Portuguese superstar follows a carefully planned diet to maintain his fitness, yet he has never hidden his love for traditional food from home. From a classic cod dish that brings back childhood memories to Armenian cuisine in Saudi Arabia, his dining choices offer a glimpse into his personal life. While his training routine leaves little room for indulgence, Ronaldo has several favourite dishes and restaurants that reflect his taste for good food.Cristiano Ronaldo's favourite food has a special connection to PortugalFor a player who spends much of his life travelling, familiar food can offer a comforting reminder of home. Ronaldo's favourite dish is reportedly Bacalhau à Brás, a traditional Portuguese meal made with salted cod, onions, thin fried potatoes and scrambled eggs.The dish is popular across Portugal, but it holds particular importance for Ronaldo because of his connection to his homeland. It is not simply another meal on his menu. It represents the flavours he grew up with in Madeira and the food culture he carried with him throughout his football career.Portuguese national team chef Hélio Loureiro revealed Ronaldo's preference during an interview with Brazilian television in 2014. He explained that the forward had a particular fondness for the traditional cod preparation. Ronaldo's mother had also spoken publicly about his love for the dish.The footballer himself has expressed his affection for cod. During an interview with EFE, when asked about his favourite food, he gave a simple answer: "Uff, ¡bacalao!"Bacalhau à Brás combines several ingredients that create a rich and satisfying meal. The salted cod provides the main flavour, while the eggs and potatoes give it a soft yet slightly crispy texture. Onions add sweetness, and olives and parsley often complete the dish.However, Ronaldo does not eat this traditional favourite every day. The meal contains fried potatoes and eggs, making it heavier than the food he usually chooses during his training routine.His regular diet places greater emphasis on fish, lean protein, vegetables, fresh fruit and whole grains. He has also spoken about enjoying fresh fish, particularly because it provides a valuable source of protein.Cristiano Ronaldo's reported favourite restaurant in Riyadh is LavashSince joining Al-Nassr in 2023, Ronaldo has made Saudi Arabia an important part of his life. His move also introduced him to a different food culture, and one Riyadh restaurant has reportedly become a favourite for him and his family.The Armenian restaurant Lavash has attracted attention after reports in May 2026 claimed that Ronaldo visits the establishment regularly. The three-storey venue features a main dining area, a private VIP room and an outdoor terrace.One detail makes the restaurant particularly interesting for football fans. Ronaldo reportedly has a favourite dish there, known as hobob or hopop.The Armenian preparation consists of fried chicken topped with pomegranate seeds and caramelised onions. The combination brings together savoury flavours with the sweetness of the fruit, creating a distinctive meal.Reports also suggest that Ronaldo enjoys Armenian appetisers and fresh salads during his visits. Although he generally avoids sugary treats, he reportedly allows himself an occasional dessert during special celebrations.His connection with Lavash also goes beyond an ordinary restaurant visit. Ronaldo and his family reportedly celebrated Georgina Rodríguez's birthday there shortly after moving to Saudi Arabia. He has since been linked to further visits.For a player who spends so much time following a strict routine, finding a restaurant that offers familiar comfort and quality food can make a difference. Lavash appears to have become one such place during his time in Riyadh.Cristiano Ronaldo's favourite restaurants around the world include Clap and PiccolinoRonaldo's restaurant choices have changed as his football career has taken him across England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia. He has enjoyed meals at several well-known establishments, often alongside his family and close friends.One of the restaurants associated with his time in Riyadh is Clap, a Japanese dining destination known for its sushi and contemporary dishes. Ronaldo and Georgina reportedly celebrated Valentine's Day there, making it one of the notable restaurants linked to the couple.The restaurant is known for its Japanese-inspired menu, including the Kyoen sushi platter and rock shrimp. Its stylish setting also makes it a popular choice for special occasions.Manchester also has a connection to Ronaldo's dining history. After returning to Manchester United in 2021, the footballer celebrated his homecoming with a family meal at Piccolino in Hale. He was accompanied by his mother, Dolores Aveiro, Georgina and his eldest son, Cristiano Jr.The Italian restaurant became part of a memorable family outing during his second spell in England. Ronaldo has also been spotted at Fortune City, a Chinese restaurant in Cheshire.His time in Turin brought another dining destination into the picture. During his Juventus years, Casa Fiore was reportedly among the restaurants he visited regularly. The establishment serves Italian and Mediterranean food, offering another example of his interest in different cuisines.Madrid also features prominently in his dining history. Cafeteria Miranda and Filandon are among the restaurants associated with his years at Real Madrid. Filandon is particularly known for its grilled meat and fish, making it an interesting choice for someone who enjoys fresh, protein-rich meals.These restaurant visits show that Ronaldo's food preferences are not limited to one country or style of cooking. articles.body:
The Detroit Lions will take on the New England Patriots in Germany this Sunday, giving international fans a taste of NFL action.

But the Lions, who are already considerably shorthanded thanks to injuries to both Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder, among others, just reported a concerning update regarding quarterback Jared Goff.

According to the latest practice report, Goff was limited in practice on Wednesday due to a chest injury.

Detroit Lions Quarterback Jared Goff Limited In Practice With A Chest Injury

According to the latest practice report, quarterback Jared Goff was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday because of a chest injury.

So far this season, Goff has been solid, throwing for 2,134 yards and 15 touchdowns with just two interceptions. During Detroit's most recent win over the Miami Dolphins , Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards with no touchdowns.

Following the retirement of Teddy Bridgewater before the season began, the Lions signed veteran Joshua Dobbs to take his place as backup quarterback.

Jared Goff Spoke About Jack Campbell's Injury

In Week 8, the Lions lost linebacker Jack Campbell to a frightening injury that left him hospitalized.

According to Goff, after Detroit's win over the Dolphins, the Lions put forward a performance that they hope would make Campbell proud.

"It was hard. It was hard," Goff said. "But I think as the week went on, you start to think about, 'What would he want? How would he want us to play?'"

"He wouldn't even want us talking about him right now. He wouldn't want us doing all this stuff about how we're going to play for him. He wouldn't want any of that. But he's a special guy to us and means a lot."

As Goff said, Campbell's injury had a rallying effect on the rest of the club.

"I think all week, certainly early in the week, it was really hard to kind of get your mind back into what we have to do. Certainly for those guys on defense, he's their nucleus. To be able to come back to work and work the way they did, and then play the way they did, and us as a team kind of rallying around each other and leaning on each other a little bit."

articles.title: Eli Raridon Features the Best 3 Tight End Streamers in Week 10 Fantasy Football
articles.summary: The top 3 tight ends to stream in Week 10 fantasy football, including Eli Raridon.
articles.body:
The tight end position differs from other fantasy football positions. The top tight ends average fewer yards per game than top wide receivers. As a result, they can be more touchdown-dependent. My rule of thumb is: find probable volume, and if they don't have it, look for huge touchdown upside in the coming weeks. Based on my analysis, the following three tight ends are streamers worth adding in Week 10.

The Bengals are on tap to play Freiermuth this Sunday. They rank second-worst in both Yards per Target Allowed and Total Yards Allowed per game to tight ends. When the two teams met in Week 3, Freiermuth had a mediocre day that hinted at better things to come.

Despite just two receptions in that Week 3 game, Freiermuth did have 30 yards. It was his second-best game this season in Yards per Reception (15.0). The point is proven that the Bengals are poor in the open field against tight ends.

Given that the Steelers will not have Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr., and that Metcalf has caught only 25% of his passes in his last two games, Freiermuth's stock has to be up this week.

Schultz has at least 4 targets and 30 yards in each of his last four games. Over his last three games, Schultz has a 19% targets-per-route run rate . Better yet, his quarterback, CJ Stroud, is red-hot.

Stroud has 16 passing touchdowns and 2 interceptions this season. This past week, he threw five touchdowns alone. In eight games played, Stroud has four with at least 312 passing yards.

So long as this Texans offense is rolling, Schultz is a considerable streamer. His opponent, the Cleveland Browns, rank 10th-worst in Fantasy Points Allowed to tight ends.

Raridon's Week 10 opponent, the Detroit Lions, have been abysmal against tight ends this season. In eight games, they've allowed tight ends 64 receptions, 704 yards, and 11 touchdowns. Over Raridon's last five games, he's recorded at least 52 yards three times.

Drake Maye has targeted the tight end 29% of the time in the red zone. In those cases, Raridon has the majority of them (6).

Among tight ends with at least a 40% route share in 2026, Raridon ranks sixth-best in both Targets per Route Run Rate and Yards per Route Run. Expect Josh McDaniels to have a game plan for his tight ends, with Raridon highlighted.

The Kansas City Chiefs reunited with rookie defensive lineman Jack Pyburn on November 11 after waiving him earlier in the day.

According to Greg Auman of FOX Sports, Pyburn cleared waivers and signed with Kansas City's practice squad mere hours after the Chiefs had initially parted ways with him.

Pyburn played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2026 preseason and was claimed off waivers by Kansas City on August 31. Formerly a member of the Chiefs' 53-man roster, Pyburn has yet to make his debut for Kansas City in the regular season.

Take a look at Auman's report on Pyburn's latest signing with the Chiefs, which was posted to his official Twitter account:

While Pyburn might not be the most well-recognized name on Kansas City's roster, the Chiefs' coaching staff must like what it has seen from the rookie pass-rusher, and fans shouldn't be surprised if the former LSU Tiger earns elevation to the team's 53-man roster at some point during the back half of the 2026 NFL regular season.

articles.title: Xavier gets tough early-season test against Mississippi State
articles.summary: After a 3-0 start, Xavier gets a litmus test matchup against Mississippi State in the Greenbrier Tip-Off Nov. 13.
articles.body:
If you're a Xavier men's basketball fan, the last month has been bliss as the Musketeers returned to the court with a revamped roster under second-year head coach Richard Pitino .

In October, Xavier won all three of its exhibition games in different ways. In November, Xavier has done what a team with NCAA Tournament aspirations should do against its buy-game opponents, winning by an average of 37.7 points after Tuesday's 100-55 blowout of Detroit Mercy.

But now, the rubber is about to meet the road. Four of Xavier's next five games are against another high-major program, beginning with an SEC test against Mississippi State in the Greenbrier Tip-Off in the cozy confines of Colonial Hall in West Virginia.

"We're gonna really learn a lot about ourselves," Pitino said.

Photos: Detroit Mercy Titans at Xavier Musketeers, 11/10

Xavier's defensive scouting report starts with Josh Hubbard

In an era full of change, Josh Hubbard has been a constant in Starkville. In Monday's win over Jackson State, Hubbard became the fourth player in program history to score 2,000-plus points. He's only 142 points away from becoming the school's all-time leading scorer.

Last season, Hubbard ranked 10th in the nation in scoring at 22.1 points per game. In three buy games thus far, Hubbard is shooting 56.3% from 3-point range and is averaging 18 points and five assists.

Whether it's slowing down Hubbard or making sure Mississippi State's complementary pieces don't beat you, Xavier will have its hands full against a team that has averaged 95.3 points through three games while shooting 52.4% from the field.

Can Xavier continue its success getting to the rim?

Xavier wants to improve on its shooting percentages from 3-point range and at the charity stripe, but the Musketeers are getting to the rim and finishing at a high percentage.

Xavier is No. 7 in KenPom in two-point shooting and boasts the seventh-tallest lineup in college basketball. That size can be advantage against a smaller Mississippi State rotation.

We'll see if Xavier gets Mike Nwoko involved early in the post. The LSU transfer is shooting 73.9% so far this season, helping Xavier rack up 160 points in the paint over three games.

Xavier is off to a stellar defensive start, holding three consecutive opponents under 30% shooting. They'll try to force misses against Mississippi State, but the Muskies need to make them one-and-done possessions. The Bulldogs haven't missed a lot, but when they do, they're creating second-chance opportunities with 48 offensive rebounds thus far. Mississippi State's offensive rebounding percentage is fourth in the country, per KenPom.

Xavier has had two great games on the glass, but Eastern Michigan's size and physicality led to a 39-33 advantage on the glass Nov. 6. Xavier won't be able to afford those lapses in the rebounding battle.

Tip : 9 p.m., Friday, Nov. 13 at Colonial Hall at The Greenbrier Resort (1,200)

Ratings : Xavier is No. 40 in KenPom and Mississippi State is No. 55.

History : Mississippi State has won four of five all-time matchups. Xavier's lone win over Mississippi State was in the second round of the 2004 NCAA Tournament in Orlando, Florida.

Head coach : Chris Jans (79-59 at Mississippi State, fifth season)

Overview : Like Xavier, Mississippi State is 3-0 after three buys games. The Bulldogs allowed 88 points in their season-opening win over Tennessee Tech. They responded by giving up a combined 101 points on just 32.7% shooting (35-for-107) in blowout wins over Northwestern State and Jackson State.

Head coach : Richard Pitino (18-18 at Xavier, second season)

Xavier vs. Mississippi State final score prediction

It'll be interesting to see what the environment is like in such a small arena. Xavier's defensive intensity and height advantage carries the Musketeers to a 4-0 start: Xavier 75, Mississippi State 70

articles.title: Will Stein confirms Jaden Smith tore his ACL; Antwan Smith could return for the postseason
articles.summary: Both players were injured in the overtime win at South Carolina.
articles.body:
Kentucky Football finally has clarity on two defenders who haven't played since the first weekend of October, and the news is mixed.

On Wednesday night's edition of The Will Stein Show presented by UK HealthCare, Stein told host Tom Leach that nickel cornerback Jaden Smith tore his ACL in the 35-34 overtime win at South Carolina and will miss the rest of the season. Linebacker Antwan Smith, who was hurt in the same game, had ankle surgery. Stein said there's a chance Smith is back for the postseason.

The weekly show is Stein's regular hour with the Voice of the Wildcats. They look back at the last game, look ahead to the next one, and take questions from fans. Tonight gave us the first real update on two guys who have been listed as out on every SEC availability report since Columbia.

Smith, a 6-foot-3, 205-pound sophomore from Charlotte, N.C., came into the year expected to back up at nickel and move around the secondary. He was slowed by an injury at the start of fall camp. Even so, defensive coordinator Jay Bateman said in August that he saw "a real future" for him.

Smith played in all five games before the injury and finished with 7 tackles (5 solo) and a tackle for loss. His best game was his last one. He had four tackles and a TFL at South Carolina before his knee buckled while he was rushing LaNorris Sellers late in the game, and he had to be helped off the field. An ACL tear in October means a long rehab, but because it happened so early in the season, he has a real chance to be ready for 2027.

Smith, a junior from Atlanta Westlake, is a 6-foot-3 linebacker with coverage skills and speed. He's also a big part of Kentucky's kick coverage. He played in all 12 games last season and had six tackles and a pass breakup. Before the injury this year, he had four tackles and an interception. He was carted off early against South Carolina, and Kentucky has kept his injury listed as undisclosed since then. Now, we know he had ankle surgery.

Injuries have been a constant for Smith in Lexington, so a possible bowl return is a good sign for a player who just hasn't been able to stay on the field.

Kentucky is 7-2. Florida comes to Kroger Field on Saturday, with Missouri and Louisville still left after that. The Cats are thin at linebacker. Nothing changes this week, since both Smiths have been out for over a month. What Stein added is a timeline. Jaden won't be back, and Antwan could be back if Kentucky's season goes past Thanksgiving weekend.

articles.title: Guardians rumors: The part of roster Cleveland is ‘intent’ on upgrading this offseason
articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians fell short in the postseason in 2026, as they were defeated by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series. While C...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Guardians fell short in the postseason in 2026, as they were defeated by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series. While Cleveland's underwhelming offense could use some help, the starting pitching also has questions of its own. According to Zack Meisel of The Athletic, the Guardians are "intent" on bringing in more starting pitching this offseason.

MLB free agency could be a path to accomplishing the goal. Trades are also in the conversation. While the Guards surely won't go and sign Tarik Skubal, or likely even Freddy Peralta, adding one or two veteran reliable hurlers to give the rotation more certainty beyond Parker Messick and Gavin Williams is realistic.

Messick finished second in American League Rookie of the Year voting , and he's also an AL Cy Young finalist. One could argue Messick should have won the AL Rookie of the Year. Meanwhile, Williams had a strong regular season but was dominant at times in the postseason. The two pitchers represent a stellar front of the rotation duo.

The rest of the starting rotation has questions, however. Foster Griffin is now a free agent. The Guardians didn't trust Tanner Bibee in the postseason . Joey Cantillo features potential but was inconsistent at times this past season.

The Guardians "pitching factory" may very well develop another star or two sooner rather than later. Nevertheless, adding one or two proven veteran hurlers will prove to be crucial come the 2027 postseason. If they had one more reliable starter this past postseason, their ALCS performance could have looked quite different.
